items.mechanism: Teoz activation-stair scheduling and future life-event history
rust_locations: crates/rustuml-render/src/sequence.rs::phase-1 lifecycle row scheduling and activation bar construction
causal_evidence: Rust still applies legacy SAME_MESSAGE_LIFECYCLE_ROW=30 when activate and deactivate attach across a note. Java Teoz gives LifeEventTile zero preferred height and constructs paint stairs separately; life_1 has Java height241 versus Rust271.

Teoz LiveBoxes.getStairs resets message ownership across standalone notes, samples per-event IGNORE_FUTURE_ACTIVATE / CONSIDERE_FUTURE_DEACTIVATE levels, and adds message callbacks as well as life events. Rust only pairs accepted open/close variations. Preexisting nested levels with repeated deactivation can therefore produce missing staircase segments even with correct horizontal bounds.

LiveBoxes.addStep adds five to a deactivation callback that collides with an already registered event ordinate. Stairs.addStep discards decreasing ordinates and drawOneLevel reopens a level when indent equals that level. Rust's legacy pairing cannot represent the same event history or repeated close timing.

The 24-case matrix was 0/24 before this packet and is 2/24 after. All 24 valid inputs, Java SVGs, final Rust SVGs and both-tier diagnostics are retained. No parse/runtime errors; no passing input regressed. The original 36-case Teoz matrix and original checker control pass.
items.disposition: Unrepaired distinct tile lifecycle model; requires a new precommitted account and coherent event/stair implementation before Teoz lifecycle parity can be accepted. The present packet does not certify this model.
